AI.tldr: MistyPilot is an LLM-driven framework for autonomous tool selection, orchestration, and parameter configuration in social robots, featuring physically interactive and socially intelligent agents with fast-slow thinking for improved task efficiency.
AI.motivation: While open APIs in social robots make customization easier, interpreting high-level user instructions, selecting appropriate tools, configuring parameters, and executing tasks reliably remain challenging for non-programmers.
AI.method: MistyPilot uses an agentic LLM-driven framework with two core components: Physically Interactive Agent (PIA) for sensor-triggered tool-driven task execution, and Socially Intelligent Agent (SIA) for emotionally aligned dialogue. It integrates a fast-slow thinking paradigm to capture user preferences, reduce latency, and improve efficiency.
AI.result: Extensive experiments using five contributed benchmark datasets demonstrate effectiveness in routing correctness, task completeness, fast-slow thinking retrieval efficiency, tool scalability, and emotion alignment.
AI.conclusion: MistyPilot successfully addresses challenges in autonomous tool selection and configuration for social robots, providing a comprehensive framework that combines physical interaction capabilities with social intelligence and efficient task execution.

title: Agentics 2.0: Logical Transduction Algebra for Agentic Data Workflows
comment: 14 pages, 4 figures
summary: Agentic AI is rapidly transitioning from research prototypes to enterprise deployments, where requirements extend to meet the software quality attributes of reliability, scalability, and observability beyond plausible text generation. We present Agentics 2.0, a lightweight, Python-native framework for building high-quality, structured, explainable, and type-safe agentic data workflows. At the core of Agentics 2.0, the logical transduction algebra formalizes a large language model inference call as a typed semantic transformation, which we call a transducible function that enforces schema validity and the locality of evidence. The transducible functions compose into larger programs via algebraically grounded operators and execute as stateless asynchronous calls in parallel in asynchronous Map-Reduce programs. The proposed framework provides semantic reliability through strong typing, semantic observability through evidence tracing between slots of the input and output types, and scalability through stateless parallel execution. We instantiate reusable design patterns and evaluate the programs in Agentics 2.0 on challenging benchmarks, including DiscoveryBench for data-driven discovery and Archer for NL-to-SQL semantic parsing, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance.

AI.tldr: Agentics 2.0 is a Python-native framework for building reliable, scalable, and observable agentic AI workflows using typed semantic transformations and parallel execution.
AI.motivation: Enterprise deployments of agentic AI require software quality attributes like reliability, scalability, and observability beyond just plausible text generation, moving from research prototypes to production systems.
AI.method: Introduces logical transduction algebra that formalizes LLM inference as typed semantic transformations (transducible functions) with schema validity and evidence locality. These functions compose via algebraically grounded operators and execute as stateless asynchronous calls in parallel Map-Reduce programs.
AI.result: The framework provides semantic reliability through strong typing, semantic observability through evidence tracing between input/output slots, and scalability through stateless parallel execution. Evaluation on DiscoveryBench and Archer benchmarks demonstrates state-of-the-art performance.
AI.conclusion: Agentics 2.0 enables building high-quality, structured, explainable, and type-safe agentic data workflows suitable for enterprise deployment, addressing key software engineering requirements through formal semantic foundations and parallel execution.

title: TreeLoc++: Robust 6-DoF LiDAR Localization in Forests with a Compact Digital Forest Inventory
comment: 25 pages, 27 figures and 15 tables
summary: Reliable localization is essential for sustainable forest management, as it allows robots or sensor systems to revisit and monitor the status of individual trees over long periods. In modern forestry, this management is structured around Digital Forest Inventories (DFIs), which encode stems using compact geometric attributes rather than raw data. Despite their central role, DFIs have been overlooked in localization research, and most methods still rely on dense gigabyte-sized point clouds that are costly to store and maintain. To improve upon this, we propose TreeLoc++, a global localization framework that operates directly on DFIs as a discriminative representation, eliminating the need to use the raw point clouds. TreeLoc++ reduces false matches in structurally ambiguous forests and improves the reliability of full 6-DoF pose estimation. It augments coarse retrieval with a pairwise distance histogram that encodes local tree-layout context, subsequently refining candidates via DBH-based filtering and yaw-consistent inlier selection to further reduce mismatches. Furthermore, a constrained optimization leveraging tree geometry jointly estimates roll, pitch, and height, enhancing pose stability and enabling accurate localization without reliance on dense 3D point cloud data. Evaluations on 27 sequences recorded in forests across three datasets and four countries show that TreeLoc++ achieves precise localization with centimeter-level accuracy. We further demonstrate robustness to long-term change by localizing data recorded in 2025 against inventories built from 2023 data, spanning a two-year interval. The system represents 15 sessions spanning 7.98 km of trajectories using only 250KB of map data and outperforms both hand-crafted and learning-based baselines that rely on point cloud maps. This demonstrates the scalability of TreeLoc++ for long-term deployment.

AI.tldr: TreeLoc++ is a global localization framework that uses Digital Forest Inventories (DFIs) instead of dense point clouds for precise tree localization in forests, achieving centimeter-level accuracy with minimal storage requirements.
AI.motivation: Current forest localization methods rely on dense, storage-intensive point clouds, while Digital Forest Inventories (DFIs) - which are central to modern forestry management - have been overlooked. There's a need for efficient, scalable localization that can operate directly on compact DFI representations for long-term forest monitoring.
AI.method: TreeLoc++ operates directly on DFIs using a discriminative representation approach. It combines coarse retrieval with pairwise distance histograms to encode local tree-layout context, followed by DBH-based filtering and yaw-consistent inlier selection to reduce mismatches. A constrained optimization leveraging tree geometry jointly estimates roll, pitch, and height for pose stability.
AI.result: The system achieves centimeter-level accuracy across 27 sequences in forests from three datasets across four countries. It demonstrates robustness to long-term change by localizing 2025 data against 2023 inventories. TreeLoc++ represents 15 sessions spanning 7.98 km using only 250KB of map data and outperforms both hand-crafted and learning-based baselines.
AI.conclusion: TreeLoc++ provides a scalable, storage-efficient solution for forest localization that eliminates dependence on dense point clouds. By leveraging DFIs as a discriminative representation, it enables precise, long-term forest monitoring with minimal data requirements, making it suitable for sustainable forest management applications.

title: $τ$-Knowledge: Evaluating Conversational Agents over Unstructured Knowledge
comment: 29 pages (10 main + 19 appendix)
summary: Conversational agents are increasingly deployed in knowledge-intensive settings, where correct behavior depends on retrieving and applying domain-specific knowledge from large, proprietary, and unstructured corpora during live interactions with users. Yet most existing benchmarks evaluate retrieval or tool use independently of each other, creating a gap in realistic, fully agentic evaluation over unstructured data in long-horizon interactions. We introduce $τ$-Knowledge, an extension of $τ$-Bench for evaluating agents in environments where success depends on coordinating external, natural-language knowledge with tool outputs to produce verifiable, policy-compliant state changes. Our new domain, $τ$-Banking, models realistic fintech customer support workflows in which agents must navigate roughly 700 interconnected knowledge documents while executing tool-mediated account updates. Across embedding-based retrieval and terminal-based search, even frontier models with high reasoning budgets achieve only $\sim$25.5% pass^1, with reliability degrading sharply over repeated trials. Agents struggle to retrieve the correct documents from densely interlinked knowledge bases and to reason accurately over complex internal policies. Overall, $τ$-Knowledge provides a realistic testbed for developing agents that integrate unstructured knowledge in human-facing deployments.

AI.tldr: τ-Knowledge extends τ-Bench to evaluate agents that must coordinate external natural-language knowledge with tool outputs in realistic fintech customer support workflows, revealing significant performance gaps even in frontier models.
AI.motivation: There's a gap in realistic evaluation of conversational agents in knowledge-intensive settings where correct behavior depends on retrieving and applying domain-specific knowledge from large, unstructured corpora during live interactions. Existing benchmarks evaluate retrieval or tool use independently, lacking fully agentic evaluation over unstructured data in long-horizon interactions.
AI.method: Introduces τ-Knowledge as an extension of τ-Bench, with a new domain called τ-Banking that models realistic fintech customer support workflows. Agents must navigate roughly 700 interconnected knowledge documents while executing tool-mediated account updates. The evaluation covers both embedding-based retrieval and terminal-based search approaches.
AI.result: Even frontier models with high reasoning budgets achieve only ~25.5% pass rate, with reliability degrading sharply over repeated trials. Agents struggle to retrieve correct documents from densely interlinked knowledge bases and to reason accurately over complex internal policies.
AI.conclusion: τ-Knowledge provides a realistic testbed for developing agents that integrate unstructured knowledge in human-facing deployments, highlighting significant challenges in coordinating knowledge retrieval with tool use in complex, knowledge-intensive environments.

title: UrbanHuRo: A Two-Layer Human-Robot Collaboration Framework for the Joint Optimization of Heterogeneous Urban Services
comment: 8 pages, 15 figures. This paper has been accepted by ICRA'26 as a regular paper
summary: In the vision of smart cities, technologies are being developed to enhance the efficiency of urban services and improve residents' quality of life. However, most existing research focuses on optimizing individual services in isolation, without adequately considering reciprocal interactions among heterogeneous urban services that could yield higher efficiency and improved resource utilization. For example, human couriers could collect traffic and air quality data along their delivery routes, while sensing robots could assist with on-demand delivery during peak hours, enhancing both sensing coverage and delivery efficiency. However, the joint optimization of different urban services is challenging due to potentially conflicting objectives and the need for real-time coordination in dynamic environments. In this paper, we propose UrbanHuRo, a two-layer human-robot collaboration framework for joint optimization of heterogeneous urban services, demonstrated through crowdsourced delivery and urban sensing. UrbanHuRo includes two key designs: (i) a scalable distributed MapReduce-based K-submodular maximization module for efficient order dispatch, and (ii) a deep submodular reward reinforcement learning algorithm for sensing route planning. Experimental evaluations on real-world datasets from a food delivery platform demonstrate that UrbanHuRo improves sensing coverage by 29.7% and courier income by 39.2% on average in most settings, while also significantly reducing the number of overdue orders.

AI.tldr: UrbanHuRo is a two-layer human-robot collaboration framework that jointly optimizes crowdsourced delivery and urban sensing services in smart cities, achieving significant improvements in sensing coverage, courier income, and delivery reliability.
AI.motivation: Existing smart city research optimizes individual urban services in isolation, missing opportunities for synergistic efficiency gains through reciprocal interactions between heterogeneous services like delivery and sensing. Current approaches fail to address conflicting objectives and real-time coordination challenges in dynamic urban environments.
AI.method: UrbanHuRo employs a two-layer human-robot collaboration framework with two key components: (1) a scalable distributed MapReduce-based K-submodular maximization module for efficient order dispatch, and (2) a deep submodular reward reinforcement learning algorithm for sensing route planning.
AI.result: Experimental evaluations on real-world food delivery datasets show UrbanHuRo improves sensing coverage by 29.7% and courier income by 39.2% on average, while significantly reducing the number of overdue orders across most settings.
AI.conclusion: UrbanHuRo successfully demonstrates that joint optimization of heterogeneous urban services through human-robot collaboration can achieve substantial efficiency gains, addressing the limitations of isolated service optimization in smart city applications.

title: A Dual-Helix Governance Approach Towards Reliable Agentic AI for WebGIS Development
comment: Paper submitted to Transactions in GIS
summary: WebGIS development requires rigor, yet agentic AI frequently fails due to five large language model (LLM) limitations: context constraints, cross-session forgetting, stochasticity, instruction failure, and adaptation rigidity. We propose a dual-helix governance framework reframing these challenges as structural governance problems that model capacity alone cannot resolve. We implement the framework as a 3-track architecture (Knowledge, Behavior, Skills) that uses a knowledge graph substrate to stabilize execution by externalizing domain facts and enforcing executable protocols, complemented by a self-learning cycle for autonomous knowledge growth. Applying this to the FutureShorelines WebGIS tool, a governed agent refactored a 2,265-line monolithic codebase into modular ES6 components. Results demonstrated a 51\% reduction in cyclomatic complexity and a 7-point increase in maintainability index. A comparative experiment against a zero-shot LLM confirms that externalized governance, not just model capability, drives operational reliability in geospatial engineering. This approach is implemented in the open-source AgentLoom governance toolkit.

AI.tldr: A dual-helix governance framework addresses LLM limitations in WebGIS development by externalizing domain knowledge and enforcing protocols, achieving significant code quality improvements.
AI.motivation: Agentic AI frequently fails in WebGIS development due to five LLM limitations: context constraints, cross-session forgetting, stochasticity, instruction failure, and adaptation rigidity. These challenges require structural governance solutions beyond model capacity alone.
AI.method: A dual-helix governance framework implemented as a 3-track architecture (Knowledge, Behavior, Skills) using a knowledge graph substrate to externalize domain facts and enforce executable protocols, complemented by a self-learning cycle for autonomous knowledge growth.
AI.result: Applied to FutureShorelines WebGIS tool, a governed agent refactored 2,265-line monolithic codebase into modular ES6 components, achieving 51% reduction in cyclomatic complexity and 7-point increase in maintainability index. Comparative experiment against zero-shot LLM confirmed governance drives operational reliability.
AI.conclusion: Externalized governance, not just model capability, drives operational reliability in geospatial engineering. The approach is implemented in the open-source AgentLoom governance toolkit.

title: Large-Language-Model-Guided State Estimation for Partially Observable Task and Motion Planning
summary: Robot planning in partially observable environments, where not all objects are known or visible, is a challenging problem, as it requires reasoning under uncertainty through partially observable Markov decision processes. During the execution of a computed plan, a robot may unexpectedly observe task-irrelevant objects, which are typically ignored by naive planners. In this work, we propose incorporating two types of common-sense knowledge: (1) certain objects are more likely to be found in specific locations; and (2) similar objects are likely to be co-located, while dissimilar objects are less likely to be found together. Manually engineering such knowledge is complex, so we explore leveraging the powerful common-sense reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Our planning and execution framework, CoCo-TAMP, introduces a hierarchical state estimation that uses LLM-guided information to shape the belief over task-relevant objects, enabling efficient solutions to long-horizon task and motion planning problems. In experiments, CoCo-TAMP achieves an average reduction of 62.7 in planning and execution time in simulation, and 72.6 in real-world demonstrations, compared to a baseline that does not incorporate either type of common-sense knowledge.

AI.tldr: CoCo-TAMP is a robot planning framework that uses LLMs to incorporate common-sense knowledge about object locations and co-location patterns, enabling efficient task and motion planning in partially observable environments.
AI.motivation: Robot planning in partially observable environments is challenging due to uncertainty. Existing planners ignore task-irrelevant objects, but common-sense knowledge about object location patterns could improve planning efficiency.
AI.method: CoCo-TAMP uses a hierarchical state estimation framework that leverages LLMs to provide common-sense knowledge about: (1) object-location likelihoods, and (2) object co-location patterns. This shapes belief over task-relevant objects for efficient task and motion planning.
AI.result: CoCo-TAMP achieves 62.7% average reduction in planning and execution time in simulation, and 72.6% reduction in real-world demonstrations compared to baseline without common-sense knowledge.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating LLM-derived common-sense knowledge about object location patterns significantly improves planning efficiency in partially observable environments, enabling practical solutions to long-horizon task and motion planning problems.

title: X-Loco: Towards Generalist Humanoid Locomotion Control via Synergetic Policy Distillation
summary: While recent advances have demonstrated strong performance in individual humanoid skills such as upright locomotion, fall recovery and whole-body coordination, learning a single policy that masters all these skills remains challenging due to the diverse dynamics and conflicting control objectives involved. To address this, we introduce X-Loco, a framework for training a vision-based generalist humanoid locomotion policy. X-Loco trains multiple oracle specialist policies and adopts a synergetic policy distillation with a case-adaptive specialist selection mechanism, which dynamically leverages multiple specialist policies to guide a vision-based student policy. This design enables the student to acquire a broad spectrum of locomotion skills, ranging from fall recovery to terrain traversal and whole-body coordination skills. To the best of our knowledge, X-Loco is the first framework to demonstrate vision-based humanoid locomotion that jointly integrates upright locomotion, whole-body coordination and fall recovery, while operating solely under velocity commands without relying on reference motions. Experimental results show that X-Loco achieves superior performance, demonstrated by tasks such as fall recovery and terrain traversal. Ablation studies further highlight that our framework effectively leverages specialist expertise and enhances learning efficiency.

AI.tldr: X-Loco is a framework for training vision-based generalist humanoid locomotion policies using synergetic policy distillation with case-adaptive specialist selection to master diverse skills including upright locomotion, fall recovery, and terrain traversal.
AI.motivation: While individual humanoid skills like upright locomotion, fall recovery, and whole-body coordination have seen strong performance, learning a single policy that masters all these skills remains challenging due to diverse dynamics and conflicting control objectives.
AI.method: X-Loco trains multiple oracle specialist policies and uses synergetic policy distillation with a case-adaptive specialist selection mechanism that dynamically leverages multiple specialist policies to guide a vision-based student policy.
AI.result: X-Loco achieves superior performance in tasks such as fall recovery and terrain traversal, and is the first framework to demonstrate vision-based humanoid locomotion jointly integrating upright locomotion, whole-body coordination and fall recovery under velocity commands without reference motions.
AI.conclusion: The framework effectively leverages specialist expertise and enhances learning efficiency, enabling acquisition of a broad spectrum of locomotion skills through dynamic specialist guidance.

title: Characterization and Correlation of Robotic Snake Scale Friction and Locomotion Speed
comment: Accepted for 9th IEEE-RAS International Conference on Soft Robotics (RoboSoft 2026), 8 pages, 7 figures
summary: Snake robots are inspired by the ability of biological snakes to move over rock, grass, leaves, soil, up trees, along pavement and more. Their ability to move in multiple distinct environments is due to their legless locomotion strategy, which combines distinct gaits with a skin that exhibits frictional anisotropy. Designing soft robotic snakes with similar capabilities requires an understanding of how this underlying frictional anisotropy should be created in engineered systems, and how variances in the frictional anisotropy ratio affect locomotion speed and direction on different surfaces. While forward and backward frictional ratios have been characterized for previous scale designs, lateral friction and the associated ratios are often overlooked. In this paper, our contributions include: (i) the development of a novel articulated pseudo-skin design that is modular, easy to construct and has removable or replaceable scales; (ii) experimental measurement of the frictional characteristics of otherwise-identical scales at varying angles of attack (15°, 25°, 35°, 45°) on different surfaces of interest (grass, bark, smooth surface, carpet);(iii) separate measurements of locomotion speed for each angle and surface. Consequently, while we observed some consistent trends between frictional coefficients and scale angle, aligning with literature and intuition, we were not able to consistently identify expected correlations between frictional ratios and locomotion speed. We conclude that either frictional ratios alone are not sufficient to predict the observed speed of a snake robot, or that specific measurement approaches are required to accurately capture these ratios.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel articulated pseudo-skin design for snake robots with replaceable scales, experimentally measures frictional characteristics at different scale angles on various surfaces, and finds that frictional ratios alone may not sufficiently predict locomotion speed.
AI.motivation: To understand how frictional anisotropy should be engineered in soft robotic snakes and how variations in frictional anisotropy ratio affect locomotion speed and direction on different surfaces, particularly addressing the overlooked lateral friction and associated ratios.
AI.method: Developed a novel articulated pseudo-skin design that is modular, easy to construct with removable/replaceable scales; experimentally measured frictional characteristics of identical scales at varying angles of attack (15°, 25°, 35°, 45°) on different surfaces (grass, bark, smooth surface, carpet); separately measured locomotion speed for each angle and surface combination.
AI.result: While consistent trends between frictional coefficients and scale angle were observed (aligning with literature and intuition), expected correlations between frictional ratios and locomotion speed were not consistently identified across different surfaces and scale angles.
AI.conclusion: Either frictional ratios alone are not sufficient to predict the observed speed of a snake robot, or specific measurement approaches are required to accurately capture these ratios for locomotion prediction.

title: Whole-Body Safe Control of Robotic Systems with Koopman Neural Dynamics
summary: Controlling robots with strongly nonlinear, high-dimensional dynamics remains challenging, as direct nonlinear optimization with safety constraints is often intractable in real time. The Koopman operator offers a way to represent nonlinear systems linearly in a lifted space, enabling the use of efficient linear control. We propose a data-driven framework that learns a Koopman embedding and operator from data, and integrates the resulting linear model with the Safe Set Algorithm (SSA). This allows the tracking and safety constraints to be solved in a single quadratic program (QP), ensuring feasibility and optimality without a separate safety filter. We validate the method on a Kinova Gen3 manipulator and a Go2 quadruped, showing accurate tracking and obstacle avoidance.

AI.tldr: A framework combining Koopman operator learning with Safe Set Algorithm enables real-time nonlinear robot control via a single quadratic program, validated on manipulator and quadruped platforms.
AI.motivation: Controlling robots with strongly nonlinear, high-dimensional dynamics is challenging because direct nonlinear optimization with safety constraints is often intractable in real time. Existing approaches may require separate safety filters or complex optimization procedures.
AI.method: Proposes a data-driven framework that learns a Koopman embedding and operator from data, then integrates the resulting linear model with the Safe Set Algorithm (SSA). This allows tracking and safety constraints to be solved in a single quadratic program (QP), ensuring feasibility and optimality without a separate safety filter.
AI.result: The method was validated on a Kinova Gen3 manipulator and a Go2 quadruped, demonstrating accurate tracking and obstacle avoidance capabilities in real-time control scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework successfully enables real-time control of nonlinear robotic systems by combining Koopman operator theory with safety guarantees through a single QP formulation, eliminating the need for separate safety filters while maintaining computational tractability.

title: HALyPO: Heterogeneous-Agent Lyapunov Policy Optimization for Human-Robot Collaboration
summary: To improve generalization and resilience in human-robot collaboration (HRC), robots must handle the combinatorial diversity of human behaviors and contexts, motivating multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). However, inherent heterogeneity between robots and humans creates a rationality gap (RG) in the learning process-a variational mismatch between decentralized best-response dynamics and centralized cooperative ascent. The resulting learning problem is a general-sum differentiable game, so independent policy-gradient updates can oscillate or diverge without added structure. We propose heterogeneous-agent Lyapunov policy optimization (HALyPO), which establishes formal stability directly in the policy-parameter space by enforcing a per-step Lyapunov decrease condition on a parameter-space disagreement metric. Unlike Lyapunov-based safe RL, which targets state/trajectory constraints in constrained Markov decision processes, HALyPO uses Lyapunov certification to stabilize decentralized policy learning. HALyPO rectifies decentralized gradients via optimal quadratic projections, ensuring monotonic contraction of RG and enabling effective exploration of open-ended interaction spaces. Extensive simulations and real-world humanoid-robot experiments show that this certified stability improves generalization and robustness in collaborative corner cases.

AI.tldr: HALyPO stabilizes multi-agent reinforcement learning for human-robot collaboration by enforcing Lyapunov stability in policy parameter space to bridge the rationality gap between heterogeneous agents.
AI.motivation: Human-robot collaboration faces combinatorial diversity of human behaviors and contexts, requiring multi-agent reinforcement learning. However, inherent heterogeneity between robots and humans creates a rationality gap - a variational mismatch between decentralized best-response dynamics and centralized cooperative ascent, causing independent policy-gradient updates to oscillate or diverge.
AI.method: Heterogeneous-agent Lyapunov policy optimization (HALyPO) establishes formal stability directly in policy-parameter space by enforcing a per-step Lyapunov decrease condition on a parameter-space disagreement metric. Unlike safe RL approaches that target state/trajectory constraints, HALyPO uses Lyapunov certification to stabilize decentralized policy learning. It rectifies decentralized gradients via optimal quadratic projections to ensure monotonic contraction of the rationality gap.
AI.result: Extensive simulations and real-world humanoid-robot experiments demonstrate that certified stability improves generalization and robustness in collaborative corner cases.
AI.conclusion: HALyPO provides a principled approach to stabilize multi-agent reinforcement learning in heterogeneous human-robot collaboration by bridging the rationality gap through Lyapunov-based policy optimization, enabling effective exploration of open-ended interaction spaces.

title: Interaction-Aware Whole-Body Control for Compliant Object Transport
summary: Cooperative object transport in unstructured environments remains challenging for assistive humanoids because strong, time-varying interaction forces can make tracking-centric whole-body control unreliable, especially in close-contact support tasks. This paper proposes a bio-inspired, interaction-oriented whole-body control (IO-WBC) that functions as an artificial cerebellum - an adaptive motor agent that translates upstream (skill-level) commands into stable, physically consistent whole-body behavior under contact. This work structurally separates upper-body interaction execution from lower-body support control, enabling the robot to maintain balance while shaping force exchange in a tightly coupled robot-object system. A trajectory-optimized reference generator (RG) provides a kinematic prior, while a reinforcement learning (RL) policy governs body responses under heavy-load interactions and disturbances. The policy is trained in simulation with randomized payload mass/inertia and external perturbations, and deployed via asymmetric teacher-student distillation so that the student relies only on proprioceptive histories at runtime. Extensive experiments demonstrate that IO-WBC maintains stable whole-body behavior and physical interaction even when precise velocity tracking becomes infeasible, enabling compliant object transport across a wide range of scenarios.

AI.tldr: Bio-inspired whole-body control separates upper-body interaction from lower-body support, using RL policy for heavy-load interactions and teacher-student distillation for proprioceptive-only runtime deployment.
AI.motivation: Cooperative object transport in unstructured environments is challenging for humanoids due to strong, time-varying interaction forces that make tracking-centric whole-body control unreliable, especially in close-contact support tasks.
AI.method: Interaction-oriented whole-body control (IO-WBC) functions as an artificial cerebellum, structurally separating upper-body interaction execution from lower-body support control. Uses trajectory-optimized reference generator for kinematic prior and RL policy for body responses under heavy-load interactions. Policy trained in simulation with randomized payload mass/inertia and external perturbations, deployed via asymmetric teacher-student distillation.
AI.result: IO-WBC maintains stable whole-body behavior and physical interaction even when precise velocity tracking becomes infeasible, enabling compliant object transport across a wide range of scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The bio-inspired, interaction-oriented approach provides reliable whole-body control for assistive humanoids in unstructured environments by separating interaction and support functions and using adaptive RL policies for robust performance under heavy loads and disturbances.

title: Cognition to Control - Multi-Agent Learning for Human-Humanoid Collaborative Transport
summary: Effective human-robot collaboration (HRC) requires translating high-level intent into contact-stable whole-body motion while continuously adapting to a human partner. Many vision-language-action (VLA) systems learn end-to-end mappings from observations and instructions to actions, but they often emphasize reactive (System 1-like) behavior and leave under-specified how sustained System 2-style deliberation can be integrated with reliable, low-latency continuous control. This gap is acute in multi-agent HRC, where long-horizon coordination decisions and physical execution must co-evolve under contact, feasibility, and safety constraints. We address this limitation with cognition-to-control (C2C), a three-layer hierarchy that makes the deliberation-to-control pathway explicit: (i) a VLM-based grounding layer that maintains persistent scene referents and infers embodiment-aware affordances/constraints; (ii) a deliberative skill/coordination layer-the System 2 core-that optimizes long-horizon skill choices and sequences under human-robot coupling via decentralized MARL cast as a Markov potential game with a shared potential encoding task progress; and (iii) a whole-body control layer that executes the selected skills at high frequency while enforcing kinematic/dynamic feasibility and contact stability. The deliberative layer is realized as a residual policy relative to a nominal controller, internalizing partner dynamics without explicit role assignment. Experiments on collaborative manipulation tasks show higher success and robustness than single-agent and end-to-end baselines, with stable coordination and emergent leader-follower behaviors.

AI.tldr: C2C: A three-layer hierarchical framework for human-robot collaboration that integrates VLM-based grounding, deliberative coordination via MARL, and whole-body control for stable contact-rich manipulation.
AI.motivation: Current vision-language-action systems for HRC emphasize reactive behaviors but lack integration of sustained System 2-style deliberation with reliable continuous control, particularly in multi-agent scenarios requiring long-horizon coordination under contact, feasibility, and safety constraints.
AI.method: Three-layer hierarchy: (1) VLM-based grounding layer for persistent scene referents and embodiment-aware affordances/constraints; (2) Deliberative skill/coordination layer using decentralized MARL cast as Markov potential game with shared potential encoding task progress; (3) Whole-body control layer for high-frequency execution with kinematic/dynamic feasibility and contact stability.
AI.result: Experiments on collaborative manipulation tasks demonstrate higher success and robustness compared to single-agent and end-to-end baselines, with stable coordination and emergent leader-follower behaviors.
AI.conclusion: C2C framework successfully bridges the gap between high-level deliberation and low-level control in human-robot collaboration, enabling stable coordination under contact constraints through explicit cognition-to-control pathway.

title: Learning Surgical Robotic Manipulation with 3D Spatial Priors
comment: CVPR26
summary: Achieving 3D spatial awareness is crucial for surgical robotic manipulation, where precise and delicate operations are required. Existing methods either explicitly reconstruct the surgical scene prior to manipulation, or enhance multi-view features by adding wrist-mounted cameras to supplement the default stereo endoscopes. However, both paradigms suffer from notable limitations: the former easily leads to error accumulation and prevents end-to-end optimization due to its multi-stage nature, while the latter is rarely adopted in clinical practice since wrist-mounted cameras can interfere with the motion of surgical robot arms. In this work, we introduce the Spatial Surgical Transformer (SST), an end-to-end visuomotor policy that empowers surgical robots with 3D spatial awareness by directly exploring 3D spatial cues embedded in endoscopic images. First, we build Surgical3D, a large-scale photorealistic dataset containing 30K stereo endoscopic image pairs with accurate 3D geometry, addressing the scarcity of 3D data in surgical scenes. Based on Surgical3D, we finetune a powerful geometric transformer to extract robust 3D latent representations from stereo endoscopes images. These representations are then seamlessly aligned with the robot's action space via a lightweight multi-level spatial feature connector (MSFC), all within an endoscope-centric coordinate frame. Extensive real-robot experiments demonstrate that SST achieves state-of-the-art performance and strong spatial generalization on complex surgical tasks such as knot tying and ex-vivo organ dissection, representing a significant step toward practical clinical deployment. The dataset and code will be released.

AI.tldr: SST is an end-to-end visuomotor policy that enables surgical robots with 3D spatial awareness by directly extracting 3D cues from stereo endoscopic images, avoiding explicit reconstruction or wrist-mounted cameras.
AI.motivation: Existing surgical robot methods have limitations: explicit 3D reconstruction leads to error accumulation and prevents end-to-end optimization, while wrist-mounted cameras interfere with robot motion and are rarely used clinically. There's a need for practical 3D spatial awareness that works with standard stereo endoscopes.
AI.method: 1) Created Surgical3D dataset with 30K stereo endoscopic image pairs with accurate 3D geometry. 2) Fine-tuned a geometric transformer to extract robust 3D latent representations from stereo images. 3) Developed a lightweight multi-level spatial feature connector (MSFC) to align these representations with robot action space in an endoscope-centric coordinate frame.
AI.result: SST achieves state-of-the-art performance and strong spatial generalization on complex surgical tasks (knot tying and ex-vivo organ dissection) in real-robot experiments, representing progress toward clinical deployment.
AI.conclusion: SST provides an end-to-end solution for 3D spatial awareness in surgical robotics that works with standard stereo endoscopes, avoiding limitations of previous approaches and showing promise for practical clinical application.

title: IROSA: Interactive Robot Skill Adaptation using Natural Language
comment: Accepted IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) journal, 8 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables, 1 listing
summary: Foundation models have demonstrated impressive capabilities across diverse domains, while imitation learning provides principled methods for robot skill adaptation from limited data. Combining these approaches holds significant promise for direct application to robotics, yet this combination has received limited attention, particularly for industrial deployment. We present a novel framework that enables open-vocabulary skill adaptation through a tool-based architecture, maintaining a protective abstraction layer between the language model and robot hardware. Our approach leverages pre-trained LLMs to select and parameterize specific tools for adapting robot skills without requiring fine-tuning or direct model-to-robot interaction. We demonstrate the framework on a 7-DoF torque-controlled robot performing an industrial bearing ring insertion task, showing successful skill adaptation through natural language commands for speed adjustment, trajectory correction, and obstacle avoidance while maintaining safety, transparency, and interpretability.

AI.tldr: A framework combining foundation models with imitation learning for open-vocabulary robot skill adaptation using a tool-based architecture that maintains safety through abstraction layers.
AI.motivation: Foundation models show impressive capabilities but haven't been sufficiently explored for robotics, especially industrial deployment. Imitation learning provides principled skill adaptation methods. Combining these approaches could enable direct application to robotics with natural language control while maintaining safety.
AI.method: Tool-based architecture with protective abstraction layer between LLM and robot hardware. Uses pre-trained LLMs to select and parameterize specific tools for skill adaptation without fine-tuning or direct model-to-robot interaction. Maintains safety, transparency, and interpretability.
AI.result: Demonstrated on 7-DoF torque-controlled robot performing industrial bearing ring insertion task. Showed successful skill adaptation through natural language commands for speed adjustment, trajectory correction, and obstacle avoidance.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables open-vocabulary skill adaptation for robotics while maintaining safety through abstraction layers, showing promise for industrial deployment without requiring model fine-tuning or direct LLM-to-robot interaction.

title: SkillVLA: Tackling Combinatorial Diversity in Dual-Arm Manipulation via Skill Reuse
comment: 16 pages
summary: Recent progress in vision-language-action (VLA) models has demonstrated strong potential for dual-arm manipulation, enabling complex behaviors and generalization to unseen environments. However, mainstream bimanual VLA formulations largely overlook the critical challenge of combinatorial diversity. Different pairings of single-arm behaviors can induce qualitatively distinct task behaviors, yet existing models do not explicitly account for this structure. We argue that effective bimanual VLAs should support skill reuse - the ability to recombine previously learned single-arm skills across novel left-right pairings - thereby avoiding the need to separately learn every possible combination. Current VLA designs entangle skills across arms, preventing such recomposition and limiting scalability. To address this limitation, we propose SkillVLA, a framework explicitly designed to enable skill reuse in dual-arm manipulation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SkillVLA substantially improves skill composition, increasing overall success rate from 0% to 51%, and achieves strong performance on cooperative and long-horizon tasks.

AI.tldr: SkillVLA enables skill reuse in dual-arm manipulation by explicitly modeling combinatorial structure, improving success rates from 0% to 51% on bimanual tasks.
AI.motivation: Current vision-language-action (VLA) models for dual-arm manipulation overlook combinatorial diversity - different pairings of single-arm behaviors create distinct task behaviors. Existing models entangle skills across arms, preventing skill reuse and requiring separate learning of every possible combination, which limits scalability.
AI.method: Proposed SkillVLA framework explicitly designed to enable skill reuse in dual-arm manipulation by supporting recombination of previously learned single-arm skills across novel left-right pairings, addressing the combinatorial structure challenge.
AI.result: SkillVLA substantially improves skill composition, increasing overall success rate from 0% to 51%, and achieves strong performance on cooperative and long-horizon tasks through effective skill reuse.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling combinatorial structure in bimanual VLA models enables skill reuse, overcoming limitations of current entangled designs and improving scalability for dual-arm manipulation tasks.

title: RVN-Bench: A Benchmark for Reactive Visual Navigation
summary: Safe visual navigation is critical for indoor mobile robots operating in cluttered environments. Existing benchmarks, however, often neglect collisions or are designed for outdoor scenarios, making them unsuitable for indoor visual navigation. To address this limitation, we introduce the reactive visual navigation benchmark (RVN-Bench), a collision-aware benchmark for indoor mobile robots. In RVN-Bench, an agent must reach sequential goal positions in previously unseen environments using only visual observations and no prior map, while avoiding collisions. Built on the Habitat 2.0 simulator and leveraging high-fidelity HM3D scenes, RVN-Bench provides large-scale, diverse indoor environments, defines a collision-aware navigation task and evaluation metrics, and offers tools for standardized training and benchmarking. RVN-Bench supports both online and offline learning by offering an environment for online reinforcement learning, a trajectory image dataset generator, and tools for producing negative trajectory image datasets that capture collision events. Experiments show that policies trained on RVN-Bench generalize effectively to unseen environments, demonstrating its value as a standardized benchmark for safe and robust visual navigation. Code and additional materials are available at: https://rvn-bench.github.io/.

AI.tldr: RVN-Bench is a collision-aware visual navigation benchmark for indoor mobile robots built on Habitat 2.0 with HM3D scenes, addressing the lack of suitable indoor benchmarks that consider collision avoidance.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks neglect collisions or are designed for outdoor scenarios, making them unsuitable for indoor visual navigation where safe collision avoidance is critical for mobile robots operating in cluttered environments.
AI.method: Built on Habitat 2.0 simulator with high-fidelity HM3D scenes, RVN-Bench defines a collision-aware navigation task requiring agents to reach sequential goals using only visual observations without prior maps. It provides tools for standardized training/benchmarking, including online RL environment, trajectory image dataset generator, and negative trajectory datasets capturing collision events.
AI.result: Policies trained on RVN-Bench generalize effectively to unseen environments, demonstrating its value as a standardized benchmark for safe and robust visual navigation.
AI.conclusion: RVN-Bench addresses the gap in collision-aware indoor visual navigation benchmarks, providing a comprehensive platform for developing and evaluating safe navigation policies that can generalize to new environments.

title: Right in Time: Reactive Reasoning in Regulated Traffic Spaces
summary: Exact inference in probabilistic First-Order Logic offers a promising yet computationally costly approach for regulating the behavior of autonomous agents in shared traffic spaces. While prior methods have combined logical and probabilistic data into decision-making frameworks, their application is often limited to pre-flight checks due to the complexity of reasoning across vast numbers of possible universes. In this work, we propose a reactive mission design framework that jointly considers uncertain environmental data and declarative, logical traffic regulations. By synthesizing Probabilistic Mission Design (ProMis) with reactive reasoning facilitated by Reactive Circuits (RC), we enable online, exact probabilistic inference over hybrid domains. Our approach leverages the Frequency of Change inherent in heterogeneous data streams to subdivide inference formulas into memoized, isolated tasks, ensuring that only the specific components affected by new sensor data are re-evaluated. In experiments involving both real-world vessel data and simulated drone traffic in dense urban scenarios, we demonstrate that our approach provides orders of magnitude in speedup over ProMis without reactive paradigms. This allows intelligent transportation systems, such as Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), to actively assert safety and legal compliance during operations rather than relying solely on preparation procedures.

AI.tldr: A reactive mission design framework combining probabilistic logic with reactive reasoning enables online exact inference for autonomous agents in traffic, achieving significant speedups over prior methods.
AI.motivation: Exact inference in probabilistic First-Order Logic offers promising but computationally expensive methods for regulating autonomous agents in shared traffic spaces. Prior methods are limited to pre-flight checks due to complexity, creating a need for online, reactive approaches that can handle uncertain environmental data and logical regulations during operations.
AI.method: The framework synthesizes Probabilistic Mission Design (ProMis) with reactive reasoning via Reactive Circuits (RC). It leverages Frequency of Change in heterogeneous data streams to subdivide inference formulas into memoized, isolated tasks, ensuring only components affected by new sensor data are re-evaluated, enabling online exact probabilistic inference over hybrid domains.
AI.result: Experiments with real-world vessel data and simulated drone traffic in dense urban scenarios demonstrate orders of magnitude speedup over ProMis without reactive paradigms, enabling intelligent transportation systems to actively assert safety and legal compliance during operations.
AI.conclusion: The reactive mission design framework enables online, exact probabilistic inference for autonomous agents in traffic, overcoming computational limitations of prior methods and allowing systems like UAS to maintain safety and compliance during operations rather than relying solely on pre-flight preparation.

title: Lightweight Visual Reasoning for Socially-Aware Robots
comment: ICRA26
summary: Robots operating in shared human environments must not only navigate, interact, and detect their surroundings, they must also interpret and respond to dynamic, and often unpredictable, human behaviours. Although recent advances have shown promise in enhancing robotic perception and instruction-following using Vision-Language Models (VLMs), they remain limited in addressing the complexities of multimodal human-robot interactions (HRI). Motivated by this challenge, we introduce a lightweight language-to-vision feedback module that closes the loop between an LLM and the vision encoder in VLMs. The module projects image-token hidden states through a gated Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) back into the encoder input, prompting a second pass that reinterprets the scene under text context. We evaluate this approach on three robotics-centred tasks: navigation in a simulated environment (Habitat), sequential scene description (Mementos-Robotics), and human-intention recognition (our HRI dataset). Results show that our method improves Qwen 2.5 (7B) by $3.3\%$ (less distance), $+0.057$ description score, and $+2.93\%$ accuracy, with less than $3\%$ extra parameters; Gemma 3 (4B) and LLaVA OV 1.5 (4B) show mixed navigation results but gains $+0.111,+0.055$ and $+10.81\%,+4.79\%$ on the latter two tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/alessioGalatolo/VLM-Reasoning-for-Robotics

AI.tldr: A lightweight language-to-vision feedback module that enables VLMs to reinterpret scenes based on text context, improving performance on robotics tasks with minimal parameter overhead.
AI.motivation: Current VLMs are limited in handling complex multimodal human-robot interactions, lacking the ability to dynamically reinterpret scenes based on contextual language cues.
AI.method: Introduces a gated MLP module that projects image-token hidden states back into the vision encoder input, enabling a second pass that reinterprets the scene under text context with less than 3% extra parameters.
AI.result: Improves Qwen 2.5 (7B) by 3.3% (navigation distance), +0.057 description score, and +2.93% accuracy; Gemma 3 (4B) and LLaVA OV 1.5 (4B) show mixed navigation results but gains on scene description and human-intention recognition tasks.
AI.conclusion: The feedback module effectively enhances VLM reasoning for robotics by enabling contextual reinterpretation of visual scenes, addressing limitations in multimodal HRI with minimal computational overhead.

title: Self-adapting Robotic Agents through Online Continual Reinforcement Learning with World Model Feedback
comment: submitted to IROS 2026
summary: As learning-based robotic controllers are typically trained offline and deployed with fixed parameters, their ability to cope with unforeseen changes during operation is limited. Biologically inspired, this work presents a framework for online Continual Reinforcement Learning that enables automated adaptation during deployment. Building on DreamerV3, a model-based Reinforcement Learning algorithm, the proposed method leverages world model prediction residuals to detect out-of-distribution events and automatically trigger finetuning. Adaptation progress is monitored using both task-level performance signals and internal training metrics, allowing convergence to be assessed without external supervision and domain knowledge. The approach is validated on a variety of contemporary continuous control problems, including a quadruped robot in high-fidelity simulation, and a real-world model vehicle. Relevant metrics and their interpretation are presented and discussed, as well as resulting trade-offs described. The results sketch out how autonomous robotic agents could once move beyond static training regimes toward adaptive systems capable of self-reflection and -improvement during operation, just like their biological counterparts.

AI.tldr: A framework for online Continual Reinforcement Learning that enables autonomous adaptation during deployment by detecting out-of-distribution events and triggering finetuning, validated on continuous control problems including simulated quadruped robots and real-world model vehicles.
AI.motivation: Learning-based robotic controllers are typically trained offline with fixed parameters, limiting their ability to cope with unforeseen changes during operation. The paper aims to move beyond static training regimes toward adaptive systems capable of self-reflection and improvement during operation, inspired by biological systems.
AI.method: Builds on DreamerV3 (model-based RL algorithm) and leverages world model prediction residuals to detect out-of-distribution events, automatically triggering finetuning. Adaptation progress is monitored using both task-level performance signals and internal training metrics, allowing convergence assessment without external supervision or domain knowledge.
AI.result: Validated on various contemporary continuous control problems, including a quadruped robot in high-fidelity simulation and a real-world model vehicle. The approach demonstrates autonomous adaptation capabilities and presents relevant metrics, their interpretation, and resulting trade-offs.
AI.conclusion: The results outline how autonomous robotic agents could move beyond static training regimes toward adaptive systems capable of self-reflection and improvement during operation, similar to biological counterparts, enabling automated adaptation to unforeseen changes during deployment.

title: Sim2Sea: Sim-to-Real Policy Transfer for Maritime Vessel Navigation in Congested Waters
summary: Autonomous navigation in congested maritime environments is a critical capability for a wide range of real-world applications. However, it remains an unresolved challenge due to complex vessel interactions and significant environmental uncertainties. Existing methods often fail in practical deployment due to a substantial sim-to-real gap, which stems from imprecise simulation, inadequate situational awareness, and unsafe exploration strategies. To address these, we propose \textbf{Sim2Sea}, a comprehensive framework designed to bridge simulation and real-world execution. Sim2Sea advances in three key aspects. First, we develop a GPU-accelerated parallel simulator for scalable and accurate maritime scenario simulation. Second, we design a dual-stream spatiotemporal policy that handles complex dynamics and multi-modal perception, augmented with a velocity-obstacle-guided action masking mechanism to ensure safe and efficient exploration. Finally, a targeted domain randomization scheme helps bridge the sim-to-real gap. Simulation results demonstrate that our method achieves faster convergence and safer trajectories than established baselines. In addition, our policy trained purely in simulation successfully transfers zero-shot to a 17-ton unmanned vessel operating in real-world congested waters. These results validate the effectiveness of Sim2Sea in achieving reliable sim-to-real transfer for practical autonomous maritime navigation.

AI.tldr: Sim2Sea is a framework for autonomous maritime navigation that bridges simulation-to-real gap through GPU-accelerated parallel simulation, dual-stream spatiotemporal policy with safety mechanisms, and domain randomization, achieving zero-shot transfer to real-world unmanned vessels.
AI.motivation: Autonomous navigation in congested maritime environments remains challenging due to complex vessel interactions, environmental uncertainties, and significant sim-to-real gaps in existing methods that fail in practical deployment due to imprecise simulation, inadequate situational awareness, and unsafe exploration strategies.
AI.method: Three key components: 1) GPU-accelerated parallel simulator for scalable and accurate maritime scenario simulation; 2) Dual-stream spatiotemporal policy handling complex dynamics and multi-modal perception with velocity-obstacle-guided action masking for safe exploration; 3) Targeted domain randomization scheme to bridge sim-to-real gap.
AI.result: Simulation results show faster convergence and safer trajectories than established baselines. The policy trained purely in simulation successfully transfers zero-shot to a 17-ton unmanned vessel operating in real-world congested waters, validating reliable sim-to-real transfer.
AI.conclusion: Sim2Sea effectively bridges the simulation-to-real gap for practical autonomous maritime navigation through its comprehensive framework combining accurate simulation, safe policy design, and domain adaptation techniques, enabling reliable deployment in congested real-world maritime environments.

title: ArthroCut: Autonomous Policy Learning for Robotic Bone Resection in Knee Arthroplasty
comment: Accepted for publication at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
summary: Despite rapid commercialization of surgical robots, their autonomy and real-time decision-making remain limited in practice. To address this gap, we propose ArthroCut, an autonomous policy learning framework that upgrades knee arthroplasty robots from assistive execution to context-aware action generation. ArthroCut fine-tunes a Qwen--VL backbone on a self-built, time-synchronized multimodal dataset from 21 complete cases (23,205 RGB--D pairs), integrating preoperative CT/MR, intraoperative NDI tracking of bones and end effector, RGB--D surgical video, robot state, and textual intent. The method operates on two complementary token families -- Preoperative Imaging Tokens (PIT) to encode patient-specific anatomy and planned resection planes, and Time-Aligned Surgical Tokens (TAST) to fuse real-time visual, geometric, and kinematic evidence -- and emits an interpretable action grammar under grammar/safety-constrained decoding. In bench-top experiments on a knee prosthesis across seven trials, ArthroCut achieves an average success rate of 86% over the six standard resections, significantly outperforming strong baselines trained under the same protocol. Ablations show that TAST is the principal driver of reliability while PIT provides essential anatomical grounding, and their combination yields the most stable multi-plane execution. These results indicate that aligning preoperative geometry with time-aligned intraoperative perception and translating that alignment into tokenized, constrained actions is an effective path toward robust, interpretable autonomy in orthopedic robotic surgery.

AI.tldr: ArthroCut is an autonomous policy learning framework that upgrades knee arthroplasty robots from assistive execution to context-aware action generation by fine-tuning a multimodal backbone on synchronized surgical data and using interpretable action grammar with safety constraints.
AI.motivation: Despite rapid commercialization of surgical robots, their autonomy and real-time decision-making capabilities remain limited in practice. Current systems primarily function as assistive execution tools rather than autonomous decision-makers with context awareness.
AI.method: Fine-tunes a Qwen-VL backbone on a self-built multimodal dataset from 21 complete cases (23,205 RGB-D pairs). Uses two complementary token families: Preoperative Imaging Tokens (PIT) for patient-specific anatomy and planned resection planes, and Time-Aligned Surgical Tokens (TAST) for real-time visual, geometric, and kinematic evidence. Emits interpretable action grammar under grammar/safety-constrained decoding.
AI.result: In bench-top experiments on a knee prosthesis across seven trials, achieves 86% average success rate over six standard resections, significantly outperforming strong baselines. Ablations show TAST is the principal driver of reliability while PIT provides essential anatomical grounding, with their combination yielding the most stable multi-plane execution.
AI.conclusion: Aligning preoperative geometry with time-aligned intraoperative perception and translating that alignment into tokenized, constrained actions is an effective path toward robust, interpretable autonomy in orthopedic robotic surgery.

title: SaFeR: Safety-Critical Scenario Generation for Autonomous Driving Test via Feasibility-Constrained Token Resampling
summary: Safety-critical scenario generation is crucial for evaluating autonomous driving systems. However, existing approaches often struggle to balance three conflicting objectives: adversarial criticality, physical feasibility, and behavioral realism. To bridge this gap, we propose SaFeR: safety-critical scenario generation for autonomous driving test via feasibility-constrained token resampling. We first formulate traffic generation as a discrete next token prediction problem, employing a Transformer-based model as a realism prior to capture naturalistic driving distributions. To capture complex interactions while effectively mitigating attention noise, we propose a novel differential attention mechanism within the realism prior. Building on this prior, SaFeR implements a novel resampling strategy that induces adversarial behaviors within a high-probability trust region to maintain naturalism, while enforcing a feasibility constraint derived from the Largest Feasible Region (LFR). By approximating the LFR via offline reinforcement learning, SaFeR effectively prevents the generation of theoretically inevitable collisions. Closed-loop experiments on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset and nuPlan demonstrate that SaFeR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a higher solution rate and superior kinematic realism while maintaining strong adversarial effectiveness.

AI.tldr: SaFeR is a safety-critical scenario generation method for autonomous driving testing that uses feasibility-constrained token resampling to balance adversarial criticality, physical feasibility, and behavioral realism.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches for safety-critical scenario generation in autonomous driving testing struggle to balance three conflicting objectives: adversarial criticality (creating challenging scenarios), physical feasibility (scenarios that obey physical laws), and behavioral realism (naturalistic driving behaviors). There's a need for a method that can effectively address all three requirements simultaneously.
AI.method: 1. Formulates traffic generation as discrete next token prediction using a Transformer-based model as a realism prior to capture naturalistic driving distributions. 2. Introduces a novel differential attention mechanism within the realism prior to capture complex interactions while mitigating attention noise. 3. Implements a feasibility-constrained token resampling strategy that induces adversarial behaviors within a high-probability trust region to maintain naturalism. 4. Enforces a feasibility constraint derived from the Largest Feasible Region (LFR), approximated via offline reinforcement learning to prevent theoretically inevitable collisions.
AI.result: Closed-loop experiments on Waymo Open Motion Dataset and nuPlan show SaFeR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving higher solution rate and superior kinematic realism while maintaining strong adversarial effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: SaFeR successfully bridges the gap in safety-critical scenario generation by effectively balancing adversarial criticality, physical feasibility, and behavioral realism through its novel feasibility-constrained token resampling approach, making it a superior solution for autonomous driving system testing.

title: Structural Action Transformer for 3D Dexterous Manipulation
comment: Accepted by CVPR
summary: Achieving human-level dexterity in robots via imitation learning from heterogeneous datasets is hindered by the challenge of cross-embodiment skill transfer, particularly for high-DoF robotic hands. Existing methods, often relying on 2D observations and temporal-centric action representation, struggle to capture 3D spatial relations and fail to handle embodiment heterogeneity. This paper proposes the Structural Action Transformer (SAT), a new 3D dexterous manipulation policy that challenges this paradigm by introducing a structural-centric perspective. We reframe each action chunk not as a temporal sequence, but as a variable-length, unordered sequence of joint-wise trajectories. This structural formulation allows a Transformer to natively handle heterogeneous embodiments, treating the joint count as a variable sequence length. To encode structural priors and resolve ambiguity, we introduce an Embodied Joint Codebook that embeds each joint's functional role and kinematic properties. Our model learns to generate these trajectories from 3D point clouds via a continuous-time flow matching objective. We validate our approach by pre-training on large-scale heterogeneous datasets and fine-tuning on simulation and real-world dexterous manipulation tasks. Our method consistently outperforms all baselines, demonstrating superior sample efficiency and effective cross-embodiment skill transfer. This structural-centric representation offers a new path toward scaling policies for high-DoF, heterogeneous manipulators.

AI.tldr: SAT introduces a structural-centric approach to dexterous manipulation by treating actions as unordered joint-wise trajectories, enabling effective cross-embodiment skill transfer for high-DoF robotic hands.
AI.motivation: Current imitation learning methods for robotic dexterity struggle with cross-embodiment skill transfer due to reliance on 2D observations and temporal-centric action representations that fail to capture 3D spatial relations and handle embodiment heterogeneity.
AI.method: Proposes Structural Action Transformer (SAT) that reframes actions as variable-length, unordered sequences of joint-wise trajectories. Uses an Embodied Joint Codebook to encode functional roles and kinematic properties, and learns to generate trajectories from 3D point clouds via continuous-time flow matching.
AI.result: SAT consistently outperforms all baselines in simulation and real-world dexterous manipulation tasks, demonstrating superior sample efficiency and effective cross-embodiment skill transfer after pre-training on large-scale heterogeneous datasets.
AI.conclusion: The structural-centric representation offers a new paradigm for scaling policies for high-DoF, heterogeneous manipulators, challenging traditional temporal-centric approaches to dexterous manipulation.

title: GarmentPile++: Affordance-Driven Cluttered Garments Retrieval with Vision-Language Reasoning
comment: ICRA2026 Accepted
summary: Garment manipulation has attracted increasing attention due to its critical role in home-assistant robotics. However, the majority of existing garment manipulation works assume an initial state consisting of only one garment, while piled garments are far more common in real-world settings. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel garment retrieval pipeline that can not only follow language instruction to execute safe and clean retrieval but also guarantee exactly one garment is retrieved per attempt, establishing a robust foundation for the execution of downstream tasks (e.g., folding, hanging, wearing). Our pipeline seamlessly integrates vision-language reasoning with visual affordance perception, fully leveraging the high-level reasoning and planning capabilities of VLMs alongside the generalization power of visual affordance for low-level actions. To enhance the VLM's comprehensive awareness of each garment's state within a garment pile, we employ visual segmentation model (SAM2) to execute object segmentation on the garment pile for aiding VLM-based reasoning with sufficient visual cues. A mask fine-tuning mechanism is further integrated to address scenarios where the initial segmentation results are suboptimal. In addition, a dual-arm cooperation framework is deployed to address cases involving large or long garments, as well as excessive garment sagging caused by incorrect grasping point determination, both of which are strenuous for a single arm to handle. The effectiveness of our pipeline are consistently demonstrated across diverse tasks and varying scenarios in both real-world and simulation environments. Project page: https://garmentpile2.github.io/.

AI.tldr: A novel garment retrieval pipeline for piled garments using vision-language reasoning and visual affordance perception to guarantee exactly one garment retrieval per attempt for downstream tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing garment manipulation works typically assume single-garment scenarios, but piled garments are far more common in real-world settings, creating a gap between research and practical applications.
AI.method: Integrates vision-language models (VLMs) for high-level reasoning with visual affordance perception for low-level actions, uses SAM2 for object segmentation on garment piles, incorporates mask fine-tuning for suboptimal segmentation, and employs dual-arm cooperation for handling large/long garments and sagging issues.
AI.result: The pipeline consistently demonstrates effectiveness across diverse tasks and varying scenarios in both real-world and simulation environments, enabling safe and clean retrieval with guaranteed single-garment retrieval per attempt.
AI.conclusion: The proposed pipeline successfully bridges the gap between single-garment manipulation research and real-world piled garment scenarios, establishing a robust foundation for downstream garment manipulation tasks through integrated vision-language reasoning and affordance perception.

title: PRAM-R: A Perception-Reasoning-Action-Memory Framework with LLM-Guided Modality Routing for Adaptive Autonomous Driving
summary: Multimodal perception enables robust autonomous driving but incurs unnecessary computational cost when all sensors remain active. This paper presents PRAM-R, a unified Perception-Reasoning-Action-Memory framework with LLM-Guided Modality Routing for adaptive autonomous driving. PRAM-R adopts an asynchronous dual-loop design: a fast reactive loop for perception and control, and a slow deliberative loop for reasoning-driven modality selection and memory updates. An LLM router selects and weights modalities using environmental context and sensor diagnostics, while a hierarchical memory module preserves temporal consistency and supports long-term adaptation. We conduct a two-stage evaluation: (1) synthetic stress tests for stability analysis and (2) real-world validation on the nuScenes dataset. Synthetic stress tests confirm 87.2% reduction in routing oscillations via hysteresis-based stabilization. Real-world validation on nuScenes shows 6.22% modality reduction with 20% memory recall while maintaining comparable trajectory accuracy to full-modality baselines in complex urban scenarios. Our work demonstrates that LLM-augmented architectures with hierarchical memory achieve efficient, adaptive multimodal perception in autonomous driving.

AI.tldr: PRAM-R is an LLM-guided multimodal routing framework for autonomous driving that reduces computational costs by adaptively selecting sensors while maintaining performance through hierarchical memory and dual-loop architecture.
AI.motivation: Current multimodal perception systems in autonomous driving incur unnecessary computational costs by keeping all sensors constantly active, even when not needed for the current driving context.
AI.method: PRAM-R uses an asynchronous dual-loop design: fast reactive loop for perception/control and slow deliberative loop for reasoning-driven modality selection. An LLM router selects and weights modalities based on environmental context and sensor diagnostics, supported by hierarchical memory for temporal consistency and long-term adaptation.
AI.result: Synthetic stress tests show 87.2% reduction in routing oscillations via hysteresis-based stabilization. Real-world validation on nuScenes demonstrates 6.22% modality reduction with 20% memory recall while maintaining comparable trajectory accuracy to full-modality baselines in complex urban scenarios.
AI.conclusion: LLM-augmented architectures with hierarchical memory can achieve efficient, adaptive multimodal perception in autonomous driving by intelligently routing sensor usage based on context while preserving performance through memory-augmented reasoning.

title: Map-Agnostic And Interactive Safety-Critical Scenario Generation via Multi-Objective Tree Search
summary: Generating safety-critical scenarios is essential for validating the robustness of autonomous driving systems, yet existing methods often struggle to produce collisions that are both realistic and diverse while ensuring explicit interaction logic among traffic participants. This paper presents a novel framework for traffic-flow level safety-critical scenario generation via multi-objective Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS). We reframe trajectory feasibility and naturalistic behavior as optimization objectives within a unified evaluation function, enabling the discovery of diverse collision events without compromising realism. A hybrid Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) and Lower Confidence Bound (LCB) search strategy is introduced to balance exploratory efficiency with risk-averse decision-making. Furthermore, our method is map-agnostic and supports interactive scenario generation with each vehicle individually powered by SUMO's microscopic traffic models, enabling realistic agent behaviors in arbitrary geographic locations imported from OpenStreetMap. We validate our approach across four high-risk accident zones in Hong Kong's complex urban environments. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves an 85\% collision failure rate while generating trajectories with superior feasibility and comfort metrics. The resulting scenarios exhibit greater complexity, as evidenced by increased vehicle mileage and CO\(_2\) emissions. Our work provides a principled solution for stress testing autonomous vehicles through the generation of realistic yet infrequent corner cases at traffic-flow level.

AI.tldr: A novel MCTS-based framework generates realistic, diverse safety-critical scenarios for autonomous vehicle testing by optimizing trajectory feasibility and naturalistic behavior, validated in Hong Kong's complex urban environments.
AI.motivation: Existing methods struggle to produce collisions that are both realistic and diverse while ensuring explicit interaction logic among traffic participants for validating autonomous driving systems.
AI.method: Multi-objective Monte Carlo Tree Search framework with trajectory feasibility and naturalistic behavior as optimization objectives, using hybrid UCB/LCB search strategy, map-agnostic design with SUMO microscopic traffic models and OpenStreetMap integration.
AI.result: Achieves 85% collision failure rate with superior feasibility and comfort metrics, generates more complex scenarios evidenced by increased vehicle mileage and CO₂ emissions, validated across four high-risk accident zones in Hong Kong.
AI.conclusion: Provides a principled solution for stress testing autonomous vehicles through generation of realistic yet infrequent corner cases at traffic-flow level.

title: VANGUARD: Vehicle-Anchored Ground Sample Distance Estimation for UAVs in GPS-Denied Environments
summary: Autonomous aerial robots operating in GPS-denied or communication-degraded environments frequently lose access to camera metadata and telemetry, leaving onboard perception systems unable to recover the absolute metric scale of the scene. As LLM/VLM-based planners are increasingly adopted as high-level agents for embodied systems, their ability to reason about physical dimensions becomes safety-critical -- yet our experiments show that five state-of-the-art VLMs suffer from spatial scale hallucinations, with median area estimation errors exceeding 50%. We propose VANGUARD, a lightweight, deterministic Geometric Perception Skill designed as a callable tool that any LLM-based agent can invoke to recover Ground Sample Distance (GSD) from ubiquitous environmental anchors: small vehicles detected via oriented bounding boxes, whose modal pixel length is robustly estimated through kernel density estimation and converted to GSD using a pre-calibrated reference length. The tool returns both a GSD estimate and a composite confidence score, enabling the calling agent to autonomously decide whether to trust the measurement or fall back to alternative strategies. On the DOTA~v1.5 benchmark, VANGUARD achieves 6.87% median GSD error on 306~images. Integrated with SAM-based segmentation for downstream area measurement, the pipeline yields 19.7% median error on a 100-entry benchmark -- with 2.6x lower category dependence and 4x fewer catastrophic failures than the best VLM baseline -- demonstrating that equipping agents with deterministic geometric tools is essential for safe autonomous spatial reasoning.
