AI.tldr: VANGUARD is a lightweight geometric perception tool that enables LLM/VLM-based agents to recover metric scale from environmental anchors (small vehicles) in GPS-denied environments, addressing spatial scale hallucinations in current VLMs.
AI.motivation: Autonomous aerial robots in GPS-denied environments lose camera metadata and telemetry, preventing metric scale recovery. Current VLMs suffer from spatial scale hallucinations (median area errors >50%), creating safety risks for LLM/VLM-based planners that need to reason about physical dimensions.
AI.method: VANGUARD uses oriented bounding boxes to detect small vehicles as environmental anchors, applies kernel density estimation to robustly estimate their modal pixel length, then converts to Ground Sample Distance (GSD) using pre-calibrated reference lengths. It returns both GSD estimate and confidence score for agent decision-making.
AI.result: On DOTA v1.5 benchmark: 6.87% median GSD error on 306 images. Integrated with SAM-based segmentation for area measurement: 19.7% median error on 100-entry benchmark, with 2.6x lower category dependence and 4x fewer catastrophic failures than best VLM baseline.
AI.conclusion: Equipping LLM-based agents with deterministic geometric tools like VANGUARD is essential for safe autonomous spatial reasoning, addressing fundamental scale hallucination issues in current VLMs for embodied systems.

title: RoboCasa365: A Large-Scale Simulation Framework for Training and Benchmarking Generalist Robots
comment: ICLR 2026; First three authors contributed equally
summary: Recent advances in robot learning have accelerated progress toward generalist robots that can perform everyday tasks in human environments. Yet it remains difficult to gauge how close we are to this vision. The field lacks a reproducible, large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation. To fill this gap, we present RoboCasa365, a comprehensive simulation benchmark for household mobile manipulation. Built on the RoboCasa platform, RoboCasa365 introduces 365 everyday tasks across 2,500 diverse kitchen environments, with over 600 hours of human demonstration data and over 1600 hours of synthetically generated demonstration data -- making it one of the most diverse and large-scale resources for studying generalist policies. RoboCasa365 is designed to support systematic evaluations for different problem settings, including multi-task learning, robot foundation model training, and lifelong learning. We conduct extensive experiments on this benchmark with state-of-the-art methods and analyze the impacts of task diversity, dataset scale, and environment variation on generalization. Our results provide new insights into what factors most strongly affect the performance of generalist robots and inform strategies for future progress in the field.

AI.tldr: RoboCasa365 is a comprehensive simulation benchmark with 365 household tasks across 2,500 kitchen environments, featuring extensive human and synthetic demonstration data to evaluate generalist robot policies.
AI.motivation: The field lacks a reproducible, large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation of generalist robots performing everyday tasks in human environments, making it difficult to gauge progress toward this vision.
AI.method: Built on the RoboCasa platform, RoboCasa365 introduces 365 everyday tasks across 2,500 diverse kitchen environments with over 600 hours of human demonstration data and over 1600 hours of synthetically generated demonstration data.
AI.result: Extensive experiments with state-of-the-art methods analyze impacts of task diversity, dataset scale, and environment variation on generalization, providing insights into factors affecting generalist robot performance.
AI.conclusion: RoboCasa365 is one of the most diverse and large-scale resources for studying generalist policies, designed to support systematic evaluations for multi-task learning, robot foundation model training, and lifelong learning, informing future progress strategies.

title: Force-Aware Residual DAgger via Trajectory Editing for Precision Insertion with Impedance Control
summary: Imitation learning (IL) has shown strong potential for contact-rich precision insertion tasks. However, its practical deployment is often hindered by covariate shift and the need for continuous expert monitoring to recover from failures during execution. In this paper, we propose Trajectory Editing Residual Dataset Aggregation (TER-DAgger), a scalable and force-aware human-in-the-loop imitation learning framework that mitigates covariate shift by learning residual policies through optimization-based trajectory editing. This approach smoothly fuses policy rollouts with human corrective trajectories, providing consistent and stable supervision. Second, we introduce a force-aware failure anticipation mechanism that triggers human intervention only when discrepancies arise between predicted and measured end-effector forces, significantly reducing the requirement for continuous expert monitoring. Third, all learned policies are executed within a Cartesian impedance control framework, ensuring compliant and safe behavior during contact-rich interactions. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world precision insertion tasks show that TER-DAgger improves the average success rate by over 37\% compared to behavior cloning, human-guided correction, retraining, and fine-tuning baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating covariate shift and enabling scalable deployment in contact-rich manipulation.

AI.tldr: TER-DAgger is a human-in-the-loop imitation learning framework that uses trajectory editing and force-aware failure anticipation to improve performance in contact-rich precision insertion tasks, reducing covariate shift and expert monitoring requirements.
AI.motivation: Imitation learning for contact-rich precision insertion tasks faces two main challenges: covariate shift (distribution mismatch between training and execution) and the need for continuous expert monitoring to recover from failures during execution, which hinders practical deployment.
AI.method: TER-DAgger combines three key components: 1) Trajectory Editing Residual Dataset Aggregation that learns residual policies through optimization-based trajectory editing to fuse policy rollouts with human corrections, 2) a force-aware failure anticipation mechanism that triggers human intervention only when discrepancies arise between predicted and measured end-effector forces, and 3) execution within a Cartesian impedance control framework for compliant and safe contact-rich interactions.
AI.result: Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world precision insertion tasks show that TER-DAgger improves the average success rate by over 37% compared to behavior cloning, human-guided correction, retraining, and fine-tuning baselines.
AI.conclusion: TER-DAgger effectively mitigates covariate shift and enables scalable deployment in contact-rich manipulation by providing consistent supervision through trajectory editing, reducing expert monitoring requirements via force-aware failure anticipation, and ensuring safe execution through impedance control.

title: HE-VPR: Height Estimation Enabled Aerial Visual Place Recognition Against Scale Variance
summary: In this work, we propose HE-VPR, a visual place recognition (VPR) framework that incorporates height estimation. Our system decouples height inference from place recognition, allowing both modules to share a frozen DINOv2 backbone. Two lightweight bypass adapter branches are integrated into our system. The first estimates the height partition of the query image via retrieval from a compact height database, and the second performs VPR within the corresponding height-specific sub-database. The adaptation design reduces training cost and significantly decreases the search space of the database. We also adopt a center-weighted masking strategy to further enhance the robustness against scale differences. Experiments on two self-collected challenging multi-altitude datasets demonstrate that HE-VPR achieves up to 6.1\% Recall@1 improvement over state-of-the-art ViT-based baselines and reduces memory usage by up to 90\%. These results indicate that HE-VPR offers a scalable and efficient solution for height-aware aerial VPR, enabling practical deployment in GNSS-denied environments. All the code and datasets for this work have been released on https://github.com/hmf21/HE-VPR.

AI.tldr: HE-VPR is a visual place recognition framework that incorporates height estimation to improve aerial VPR by decoupling height inference from place recognition, using a shared frozen DINOv2 backbone with lightweight adapter branches, achieving better performance with reduced memory usage.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of visual place recognition in aerial scenarios with varying altitudes, where traditional VPR methods struggle with scale differences. The motivation is to create a scalable and efficient solution for GNSS-denied environments by incorporating height information to reduce search space and improve recognition accuracy.
AI.method: HE-VPR uses a frozen DINOv2 backbone shared between height estimation and place recognition modules. Two lightweight bypass adapter branches are added: one estimates height partition via retrieval from a compact height database, and the other performs VPR within the corresponding height-specific sub-database. A center-weighted masking strategy enhances robustness against scale differences.
AI.result: Experiments on two self-collected multi-altitude datasets show HE-VPR achieves up to 6.1% Recall@1 improvement over state-of-the-art ViT-based baselines and reduces memory usage by up to 90%.
AI.conclusion: HE-VPR provides a scalable and efficient solution for height-aware aerial visual place recognition, enabling practical deployment in GNSS-denied environments through its decoupled architecture and efficient adaptation design.

title: Swimming Under Constraints: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Framework for Quadrupedal Bio-Inspired Propulsion
summary: Bio-inspired aquatic propulsion offers high thrust and maneuverability but is prone to destabilizing forces such as lift fluctuations, which are further amplified by six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) fluid coupling. We formulate quadrupedal swimming as a constrained optimization problem that maximizes forward thrust while minimizing destabilizing fluctuations. Our proposed framework, Accelerated Constrained Proximal Policy Optimization with a PID-regulated Lagrange multiplier (ACPPO-PID), enforces constraints with a PID-regulated Lagrange multiplier, accelerates learning via conditional asymmetric clipping, and stabilizes updates through cycle-wise geometric aggregation. Initialized with imitation learning and refined through on-hardware towing-tank experiments, ACPPO-PID produces control policies that transfer effectively to quadrupedal free-swimming trials. Results demonstrate improved thrust efficiency, reduced destabilizing forces, and faster convergence compared with state-of-the-art baselines, underscoring the importance of constraint-aware safe RL for robust and generalizable bio-inspired locomotion in complex fluid environments.

AI.tldr: ACPPO-PID framework for quadrupedal swimming optimization that maximizes thrust while minimizing destabilizing forces using constraint-aware reinforcement learning with PID-regulated Lagrange multipliers.
AI.motivation: Bio-inspired aquatic propulsion offers high thrust and maneuverability but suffers from destabilizing forces like lift fluctuations, which are amplified by 6-DoF fluid coupling. Existing approaches lack constraint-aware optimization for stable swimming.
AI.method: Formulates quadrupedal swimming as constrained optimization problem. Proposes ACPPO-PID framework with: 1) PID-regulated Lagrange multiplier for constraint enforcement, 2) conditional asymmetric clipping for accelerated learning, 3) cycle-wise geometric aggregation for update stabilization. Uses imitation learning initialization and on-hardware towing-tank experiments for refinement.
AI.result: Demonstrates improved thrust efficiency, reduced destabilizing forces, and faster convergence compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Control policies transfer effectively to quadrupedal free-swimming trials.
AI.conclusion: ACPPO-PID enables robust and generalizable bio-inspired locomotion in complex fluid environments, highlighting the importance of constraint-aware safe reinforcement learning for aquatic propulsion systems.

title: Modeling and Control of a Pneumatic Soft Robotic Catheter Using Neural Koopman Operators
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Accepted to IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026
summary: Catheter-based interventions are widely used for the diagnosis and treatment of cardiac diseases. Recently, robotic catheters have attracted attention for their ability to improve precision and stability over conventional manual approaches. However, accurate modeling and control of soft robotic catheters remain challenging due to their complex, nonlinear behavior. The Koopman operator enables lifting the original system data into a linear "lifted space", offering a data-driven framework for predictive control; however, manually chosen basis functions in the lifted space often oversimplify system behaviors and degrade control performance. To address this, we propose a neural network-enhanced Koopman operator framework that jointly learns the lifted space representation and Koopman operator in an end-to-end manner. Moreover, motivated by the need to minimize radiation exposure during X-ray fluoroscopy in cardiac ablation, we investigate open-loop control strategies using neural Koopman operators to reliably reach target poses without continuous imaging feedback. The proposed method is validated in two experimental scenarios: interactive position control and a simulated cardiac ablation task using an atrium-like cavity. Our approach achieves average errors of 2.1 +- 0.4 mm in position and 4.9 +- 0.6 degrees in orientation, outperforming not only model-based baselines but also other Koopman variants in targeting accuracy and efficiency. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework for advancing soft robotic catheter systems and improving catheter-based interventions.

AI.tldr: Neural network-enhanced Koopman operator framework for soft robotic catheter control achieves 2.1±0.4 mm position and 4.9±0.6° orientation errors, outperforming model-based and other Koopman methods.
AI.motivation: Robotic catheters improve precision in cardiac interventions but face challenges in modeling nonlinear behavior. Traditional Koopman operator approaches with manually chosen basis functions oversimplify system dynamics and degrade control performance. Additionally, minimizing radiation exposure during X-ray fluoroscopy motivates open-loop control strategies.
AI.method: Proposed neural network-enhanced Koopman operator framework that jointly learns lifted space representation and Koopman operator in end-to-end manner. Investigated open-loop control strategies using neural Koopman operators to reach target poses without continuous imaging feedback.
AI.result: Achieved average errors of 2.1 ± 0.4 mm in position and 4.9 ± 0.6 degrees in orientation. Outperformed model-based baselines and other Koopman variants in targeting accuracy and efficiency. Validated in interactive position control and simulated cardiac ablation task using atrium-like cavity.
AI.conclusion: The neural Koopman operator framework advances soft robotic catheter systems by providing accurate nonlinear modeling and enabling radiation-reducing open-loop control, with potential to improve catheter-based cardiac interventions.

title: HBRB-BoW: A Retrained Bag-of-Words Vocabulary for ORB-SLAM via Hierarchical BRB-KMeans
summary: In visual simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), the quality of the visual vocabulary is fundamental to the system's ability to represent environments and recognize locations. While ORB-SLAM is a widely used framework, its binary vocabulary, trained through the k-majority-based bag-of-words (BoW) approach, suffers from inherent precision loss. The inability of conventional binary clustering to represent subtle feature distributions leads to the degradation of visual words, a problem that is compounded as errors accumulate and propagate through the hierarchical tree structure. To address these structural deficiencies, this paper proposes hierarchical binary-to-real-and-back (HBRB)-BoW, a refined hierarchical binary vocabulary training algorithm. By integrating a global real-valued flow within the hierarchical clustering process, our method preserves high-fidelity descriptor information until the final binarization at the leaf nodes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach yields a more discriminative and well-structured vocabulary than traditional methods, significantly enhancing the representational integrity of the visual dictionary in complex environments. Furthermore, replacing the default ORB-SLAM vocabulary file with our HBRB-BoW file is expected to improve performance in loop closing and relocalization tasks.

AI.tldr: HBRB-BoW: A hierarchical binary vocabulary training algorithm that integrates real-valued flow to preserve descriptor fidelity, improving visual SLAM's loop closing and relocalization performance.
AI.motivation: ORB-SLAM's binary vocabulary suffers from precision loss due to conventional binary clustering's inability to represent subtle feature distributions, causing degradation of visual words that accumulates through the hierarchical tree structure.
AI.method: Proposes hierarchical binary-to-real-and-back (HBRB)-BoW algorithm that integrates global real-valued flow within hierarchical clustering, preserving high-fidelity descriptor information until final binarization at leaf nodes.
AI.result: The approach yields more discriminative and well-structured vocabulary than traditional methods, significantly enhancing representational integrity of visual dictionary in complex environments.
AI.conclusion: Replacing default ORB-SLAM vocabulary with HBRB-BoW file is expected to improve performance in loop closing and relocalization tasks by addressing structural deficiencies of conventional binary vocabulary training.

title: Learning Hip Exoskeleton Control Policy via Predictive Neuromusculoskeletal Simulation
summary: Developing exoskeleton controllers that generalize across diverse locomotor conditions typically requires extensive motion-capture data and biomechanical labeling, limiting scalability beyond instrumented laboratory settings. Here, we present a physics-based neuromusculoskeletal learning framework that trains a hip-exoskeleton control policy entirely in simulation, without motion-capture demonstrations, and deploys it on hardware via policy distillation. A reinforcement learning teacher policy is trained using a muscle-synergy action prior over a wide range of walking speeds and slopes through a two-stage curriculum, enabling direct comparison between assisted and no-exoskeleton conditions. In simulation, exoskeleton assistance reduces mean muscle activation by up to 3.4% and mean positive joint power by up to 7.0% on level ground and ramp ascent, with benefits increasing systematically with walking speed. On hardware, the assistance profiles learned in simulation are preserved across matched speed-slope conditions (r: 0.82, RMSE: 0.03 Nm/kg), providing quantitative evidence of sim-to-real transfer without additional hardware tuning. These results demonstrate that physics-based neuromusculoskeletal simulation can serve as a practical and scalable foundation for exoskeleton controller development, substantially reducing experimental burden during the design phase.

AI.tldr: Physics-based neuromusculoskeletal learning framework trains hip-exoskeleton control policy entirely in simulation without motion-capture data, achieves successful sim-to-real transfer with preserved assistance profiles.
AI.motivation: Current exoskeleton controller development requires extensive motion-capture data and biomechanical labeling, limiting scalability beyond laboratory settings. There's a need for methods that reduce experimental burden while maintaining generalization across diverse locomotor conditions.
AI.method: Physics-based neuromusculoskeletal learning framework using reinforcement learning with muscle-synergy action prior. Two-stage curriculum training across walking speeds and slopes in simulation, followed by policy distillation for hardware deployment without additional tuning.
AI.result: In simulation: 3.4% reduction in mean muscle activation and 7.0% reduction in mean positive joint power on level ground/ramp ascent, with benefits increasing with speed. On hardware: preserved assistance profiles across matched conditions (r: 0.82, RMSE: 0.03 Nm/kg), demonstrating successful sim-to-real transfer.
AI.conclusion: Physics-based neuromusculoskeletal simulation provides a practical and scalable foundation for exoskeleton controller development, substantially reducing experimental burden while enabling effective sim-to-real transfer without hardware tuning.

title: GSeg3D: A High-Precision Grid-Based Algorithm for Safety-Critical Ground Segmentation in LiDAR Point Clouds
summary: Ground segmentation in point cloud data is the process of separating ground points from non-ground points. This task is fundamental for perception in autonomous driving and robotics, where safety and reliable operation depend on the precise detection of obstacles and navigable surfaces. Existing methods often fall short of the high precision required in safety-critical environments, leading to false detections that can compromise decision-making. In this work, we present a ground segmentation approach designed to deliver consistently high precision, supporting the stringent requirements of autonomous vehicles and robotic systems operating in real-world, safety-critical scenarios.

AI.tldr: A ground segmentation method for point clouds that prioritizes high precision for safety-critical autonomous driving and robotics applications.
AI.motivation: Existing ground segmentation methods lack the high precision needed for safety-critical environments like autonomous driving, where false detections can compromise safety and decision-making.
AI.method: The paper presents a ground segmentation approach designed specifically for high precision requirements in real-world, safety-critical scenarios.
AI.result: The method delivers consistently high precision, meeting stringent requirements for autonomous vehicles and robotic systems.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach addresses the precision gap in ground segmentation for safety-critical applications, supporting reliable operation in autonomous driving and robotics.

title: AMP2026: A Multi-Platform Marine Robotics Dataset for Tracking and Mapping
summary: Marine environments present significant challenges for perception and autonomy due to dynamic surfaces, limited visibility, and complex interactions between aerial, surface, and submerged sensing modalities. This paper introduces the Aerial Marine Perception Dataset (AMP2026), a multi-platform marine robotics dataset collected across multiple field deployments designed to support research in two primary areas: multi-view tracking and marine environment mapping. The dataset includes synchronized data from aerial drones, boat-mounted cameras, and submerged robotic platforms, along with associated localization and telemetry information. The goal of this work is to provide a publicly available dataset enabling research in marine perception and multi-robot observation scenarios. This paper describes the data collection methodology, sensor configurations, dataset organization, and intended research tasks supported by the dataset.

AI.tldr: AMP2026 is a multi-platform marine robotics dataset with synchronized aerial, surface, and submerged sensor data for multi-view tracking and marine environment mapping research.
AI.motivation: Marine environments pose significant perception challenges due to dynamic surfaces, limited visibility, and complex interactions between different sensing modalities, creating a need for comprehensive datasets to advance marine robotics research.
AI.method: The dataset was collected across multiple field deployments using synchronized aerial drones, boat-mounted cameras, and submerged robotic platforms, with associated localization and telemetry information, following a systematic data collection methodology.
AI.result: The Aerial Marine Perception Dataset (AMP2026) provides publicly available synchronized multi-platform marine robotics data supporting research in multi-view tracking and marine environment mapping.
AI.conclusion: AMP2026 enables research in marine perception and multi-robot observation scenarios by providing comprehensive synchronized data from aerial, surface, and submerged platforms, addressing the unique challenges of marine environments.

title: RoboLight: A Dataset with Linearly Composable Illumination for Robotic Manipulation
summary: In this paper, we introduce RoboLight, the first real-world robotic manipulation dataset capturing synchronized episodes under systematically varied lighting conditions. RoboLight consists of two components. (a) RoboLight-Real contains 2,800 real-world episodes collected in our custom Light Cube setup, a calibrated system equipped with eight programmable RGB LED lights. It includes structured illumination variation along three independently controlled dimensions: color, direction, and intensity. Each dimension is paired with a dedicated task featuring objects of diverse geometries and materials to induce perceptual challenges. All image data are recorded in high-dynamic-range (HDR) format to preserve radiometric accuracy. Leveraging the linearity of light transport, we introduce (b) RoboLight-Synthetic, comprising 196,000 episodes synthesized through interpolation in the HDR image space of RoboLight-Real. In principle, RoboLight-Synthetic can be arbitrarily expanded by refining the interpolation granularity. We further verify the dataset quality through qualitative analysis and real-world policy roll-outs, analyzing task difficulty, distributional diversity, and the effectiveness of synthesized data. We additionally demonstrate three representative use cases of the proposed dataset. The full dataset, along with the system software and hardware design, will be released as open-source to support continued research.

AI.tldr: RoboLight is the first real-world robotic manipulation dataset with synchronized episodes under systematically varied lighting conditions, featuring both real (2,800 episodes) and synthetic (196,000 episodes) components collected in a calibrated Light Cube setup.
AI.motivation: To address the lack of real-world robotic manipulation datasets that systematically vary lighting conditions, which is crucial for developing robust perception systems that can handle diverse illumination scenarios in practical applications.
AI.method: Developed a custom Light Cube setup with eight programmable RGB LED lights to collect RoboLight-Real dataset with structured illumination variation along color, direction, and intensity dimensions. Used HDR imaging for radiometric accuracy, then synthesized RoboLight-Synthetic dataset through interpolation in HDR image space leveraging light transport linearity.
AI.result: Created a comprehensive dataset with 2,800 real episodes and 196,000 synthetic episodes, featuring three dedicated tasks with diverse object geometries and materials. Demonstrated dataset quality through qualitative analysis, real-world policy roll-outs, and three representative use cases.
AI.conclusion: RoboLight provides the first systematic real-world lighting variation dataset for robotic manipulation, enabling research on illumination-robust perception systems. The dataset is expandable through interpolation and will be released as open-source with full system design.

title: OmniPlanner: Universal Exploration and Inspection Path Planning across Robot Morphologies
comment: The code for this paper is open-sourced and released at: https://github.com/ntnu-arl/gbplanner_ros/tree/gbplanner3
summary: Autonomous robotic systems are increasingly deployed for mapping, monitoring, and inspection in complex and unstructured environments. However, most existing path planning approaches remain domain-specific (i.e., either on air, land, or sea), limiting their scalability and cross-platform applicability. This article presents OmniPlanner, a unified planning framework for autonomous exploration and inspection across aerial, ground, and underwater robots. The method integrates volumetric exploration and viewpoint-based inspection, alongside target reach behaviors within a single modular architecture, complemented by a platform abstraction layer that captures morphology-specific sensing, traversability and motion constraints. This enables the same planning strategy to generalize across distinct mobility domains with minimal retuning. The framework is validated through extensive simulation studies and field deployments in underground mines, industrial facilities, forests, submarine bunkers, and structured outdoor environments. Across these diverse scenarios, OmniPlanner demonstrates robust performance, consistent cross-domain generalization, and improved exploration and inspection efficiency compared to representative state-of-the-art baselines.

AI.tldr: OmniPlanner is a unified planning framework for autonomous exploration and inspection across aerial, ground, and underwater robots, enabling cross-domain generalization with minimal retuning.
AI.motivation: Existing path planning approaches are domain-specific (air, land, or sea), limiting scalability and cross-platform applicability for autonomous robotic systems in complex environments.
AI.method: Integrates volumetric exploration, viewpoint-based inspection, and target reach behaviors within a single modular architecture with a platform abstraction layer that captures morphology-specific sensing, traversability, and motion constraints.
AI.result: Validated through extensive simulation studies and field deployments in diverse environments (underground mines, industrial facilities, forests, submarine bunkers, structured outdoor environments), demonstrating robust performance, consistent cross-domain generalization, and improved exploration/inspection efficiency compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
AI.conclusion: OmniPlanner provides a unified planning framework that enables autonomous robots to operate effectively across different mobility domains with minimal retuning, addressing the limitations of domain-specific approaches.

title: Compliant In-hand Rolling Manipulation Using Tactile Sensing
summary: We investigate in-hand rolling manipulation using a multifingered robot hand, where each finger is compliant and equipped with a tactile fingertip providing contact location and wrench information. We derive the equations of motion for compliant quasistatic in-hand rolling manipulation and formulate a fingertip rolling manipulation controller for multiple fingers to achieve a desired object twist within a grasp. The contact mechanics are demonstrated in simulation and the controller is tested on an experimental robot system.

AI.tldr: A multifingered robot hand with compliant fingers and tactile fingertips performs in-hand rolling manipulation using a derived controller based on contact mechanics and compliant quasistatic equations.
AI.motivation: To enable precise in-hand rolling manipulation using multifingered robot hands with compliant fingers and tactile sensing capabilities for improved dexterity and control.
AI.method: Derived equations of motion for compliant quasistatic in-hand rolling manipulation, formulated a fingertip rolling manipulation controller for multiple fingers to achieve desired object twist, and implemented contact mechanics in simulation.
AI.result: The controller was successfully tested on an experimental robot system after demonstrating contact mechanics in simulation.
AI.conclusion: The approach enables effective in-hand rolling manipulation using compliant multifingered robot hands with tactile sensing, providing a framework for precise object manipulation within grasps.

title: Perception-Aware Time-Optimal Planning for Quadrotor Waypoint Flight
summary:
Agile quadrotor flight pushes the limits of control, actuation, and onboard perception. While time-optimal trajectory planning has been extensively studied, existing approaches typically neglect the tight coupling between vehicle dynamics, environmental geometry, and the visual requirements of onboard state estimation. As a result, trajectories that are dynamically feasible may fail in closed-loop execution due to degraded visual quality. This paper introduces a unified time-optimal trajectory optimization framework for vision-based quadrotors that explicitly incorporates perception constraints alongside full nonlinear dynamics, rotor actuation limits, aerodynamic effects, camera field-of-view constraints, and convex geometric gate representations.
  The proposed formulation solves minimum-time lap trajectories for arbitrary racetracks with diverse gate shapes and orientations, while remaining numerically robust and computationally efficient. We derive an information-theoretic position uncertainty metric to quantify visual state-estimation quality and integrate it into the planner through three perception objectives: position uncertainty minimization, sequential field-of-view constraints, and look-ahead alignment. This enables systematic exploration of the trade-offs between speed and perceptual reliability.
  To accurately track the resulting perception-aware trajectories, we develop a model predictive contouring tracking controller that separates lateral and progress errors. Experiments demonstrate real-world flight speeds up to 9.8 m/s with 0.07 m average tracking error, and closed-loop success rates improved from 55% to 100% on a challenging Split-S course. The proposed system provides a scalable benchmark for studying the fundamental limits of perception-aware, time-optimal autonomous flight.

AI.tldr: Unified time-optimal trajectory optimization for vision-based quadrotors incorporating perception constraints, dynamics, actuation limits, and gate geometry to achieve high-speed autonomous flight with improved reliability.
AI.motivation: Existing time-optimal trajectory planning approaches neglect the coupling between vehicle dynamics, environmental geometry, and visual requirements for onboard state estimation, causing dynamically feasible trajectories to fail in closed-loop execution due to degraded visual quality.
AI.method: Unified time-optimal trajectory optimization framework incorporating perception constraints, full nonlinear dynamics, rotor actuation limits, aerodynamic effects, camera field-of-view constraints, and convex geometric gate representations. Uses information-theoretic position uncertainty metric with three perception objectives: uncertainty minimization, sequential field-of-view constraints, and look-ahead alignment. Implements model predictive contouring tracking controller separating lateral and progress errors.
AI.result: Real-world flight speeds up to 9.8 m/s with 0.07 m average tracking error, closed-loop success rates improved from 55% to 100% on challenging Split-S course, demonstrating systematic trade-off exploration between speed and perceptual reliability.
AI.conclusion: The proposed system provides a scalable benchmark for studying fundamental limits of perception-aware, time-optimal autonomous flight by explicitly addressing the critical coupling between perception quality and dynamic feasibility in agile quadrotor navigation.

title: Gaussian Mixture-Based Inverse Perception Contract for Uncertainty-Aware Robot Navigation
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Accepted to ACC 2026 (American Control Conference)
summary: Reliable navigation in cluttered environments requires perception outputs that are not only accurate but also equipped with uncertainty sets suitable for safe control. An inverse perception contract (IPC) provides such a connection by mapping perceptual estimates to sets that contain the ground truth with high confidence. Existing IPC formulations, however, instantiate uncertainty as a single ellipsoidal set and rely on deterministic trust scores to guide robot motion. Such a representation cannot capture the multi-modal and irregular structure of fine-grained perception errors, often resulting in over-conservative sets and degraded navigation performance. In this work, we introduce Gaussian Mixture-based Inverse Perception Contract (GM-IPC), which extends IPC to represent uncertainty with unions of ellipsoidal confidence sets derived from Gaussian mixture models. This design moves beyond deterministic single-set abstractions, enabling fine-grained, multi-modal, and non-convex error structures to be captured with formal guarantees. A learning framework is presented that trains GM-IPC to account for probabilistic inclusion, distribution matching, and empty-space penalties, ensuring both validity and compactness of the predicted sets. We further show that the resulting uncertainty characterizations can be leveraged in downstream planning frameworks for real-time safe navigation, enabling less conservative and more adaptive robot motion while preserving safety in a probabilistic manner.

AI.tldr: GM-IPC extends inverse perception contracts to represent uncertainty using Gaussian mixture models, enabling multi-modal, non-convex confidence sets for less conservative safe navigation.
AI.motivation: Existing inverse perception contracts use single ellipsoidal uncertainty sets with deterministic trust scores, which cannot capture multi-modal and irregular perception error structures, leading to over-conservative sets and degraded navigation performance.
AI.method: Introduces Gaussian Mixture-based Inverse Perception Contract (GM-IPC) that represents uncertainty with unions of ellipsoidal confidence sets derived from Gaussian mixture models. A learning framework trains GM-IPC to account for probabilistic inclusion, distribution matching, and empty-space penalties.
AI.result: GM-IPC enables fine-grained, multi-modal, and non-convex error structures to be captured with formal guarantees, producing both valid and compact predicted uncertainty sets.
AI.conclusion: The resulting uncertainty characterizations can be leveraged in downstream planning frameworks for real-time safe navigation, enabling less conservative and more adaptive robot motion while preserving safety in a probabilistic manner.

title: Tendon Force Modeling for Sim2Real Transfer of Reinforcement Learning Policies for Tendon-Driven Robots
comment: preprint
summary: Robots which make use of soft or compliant inter- actions often leverage tendon-driven actuation which enables actuators to be placed more flexibly, and compliance to be maintained. However, controlling complex tendon systems is challenging. Simulation paired with reinforcement learning (RL) could be enable more complex behaviors to be generated. Such methods rely on torque and force-based simulation roll- outs which are limited by the sim-to-real gap, stemming from the actuator and system dynamics, resulting in poor transfer of RL policies onto real robots. To address this, we propose a method to model the tendon forces produced by typical servo motors, focusing specifically on the transfer of RL policies for a tendon driven finger. Our approach extends existing data- driven techniques by leveraging contextual history and a novel data collection test-bench. This test-bench allows us to capture tendon forces undergo contact-rich interactions typical of real- world manipulation. We then utilize our force estimation model in a GPU-accelerated tendon force-driven rigid body simulation to train RL-based controllers. Our transformer-based model is capable of predicting tendon forces within 3% of the maximum motor force and is robot-agnostic. By integrating our learned model into simulation, we reduce the sim-to-real gap for test trajectories by 41%. RL-based controller trained with our model achieves a 50% improvement in fingertip pose tracking tasks on real tendon-driven robotic fingers. This approach is generalizable to different actuators and robot systems, and can enable RL policies to be used widely across tendon systems, advancing capabilities of dexterous manipulators and soft robots.

AI.tldr: A method for modeling tendon forces in tendon-driven robots using a transformer-based model and GPU-accelerated simulation to reduce sim-to-real gap and improve RL policy transfer.
AI.motivation: Controlling complex tendon-driven systems is challenging due to the sim-to-real gap in force-based simulations, which stems from actuator and system dynamics, resulting in poor transfer of RL policies to real robots.
AI.method: Proposes a tendon force modeling method using contextual history and a novel data collection test-bench to capture tendon forces during contact-rich interactions. Uses a transformer-based model to predict tendon forces, integrated into GPU-accelerated tendon force-driven rigid body simulation for RL training.
AI.result: Transformer-based model predicts tendon forces within 3% of maximum motor force and is robot-agnostic. Reduces sim-to-real gap by 41% for test trajectories. RL controller achieves 50% improvement in fingertip pose tracking on real tendon-driven robotic fingers.
AI.conclusion: The approach is generalizable to different actuators and robot systems, enabling wider use of RL policies across tendon systems and advancing capabilities of dexterous manipulators and soft robots.

title: A Soft Robotic Demonstration in the Stratospher
summary: Machines designed for operation in Space, as well as other extreme environments, need to be both resilient and adaptable when mission parameters change. Soft robots offer advantages in adaptability, but most lack resilience to the pressure and temperature extremes found as close as the Stratosphere. Dielectric elastomer actuators overcome some of those limitations when built as solid state compliant capacitors capable of converting electrical energy into mechanical work, but the elastomer resilience limits the device's operating window. Here we present a crosslinking mechanism for silicone elastomers under ultraviolet light using trimethyl(methylcyclopentadienyl)platinum(IV) as a catalyst to react hydrosilane to vinyl groups. The formation of carbon-carbon bonds enables fast processing under UV light and exceptional electro-mechanical performance in dielectric elastomer actuators. The material resilience advantage is demonstrated in controlled experiments at -40° and 120° C, as well as near vacuum, in comparison with state-of-the-art acrylic and silicone chemistries. Fully autonomous systems controlling grippers made with the novel silicone were integrated into payloads for high altitude balloon testing. Two stratospheric balloon missions were carried out and demonstrated DEAs as a viable soft robotic technology under space-like conditions (as high as 23.6 km elevation, at <0.05 atm and -55° C). The combinations of chemical building blocks and catalyst can be further expanded to address other challenges for silicones, including adhesion and additive manufacturing.

AI.tldr: UV-curable silicone elastomer with Pt catalyst enables high-performance dielectric elastomer actuators resilient to extreme temperatures and vacuum, validated in stratospheric balloon missions.
AI.motivation: Space and extreme environment machines require resilience and adaptability. Soft robots offer adaptability but lack resilience to pressure/temperature extremes. Dielectric elastomer actuators have limitations due to elastomer resilience constraints.
AI.method: Developed UV-crosslinking mechanism for silicone elastomers using trimethyl(methylcyclopentadienyl)platinum(IV) catalyst to react hydrosilane to vinyl groups, forming carbon-carbon bonds for fast processing and exceptional electro-mechanical performance.
AI.result: Material demonstrated resilience at -40°C and 120°C, near vacuum conditions. Outperformed state-of-the-art acrylic and silicone chemistries. Autonomous gripper systems with novel silicone were tested in two stratospheric balloon missions at 23.6 km elevation (<0.05 atm, -55°C), proving viability under space-like conditions.
AI.conclusion: UV-curable silicone enables resilient dielectric elastomer actuators for extreme environments. The chemical approach can be expanded to address other silicone challenges like adhesion and additive manufacturing, demonstrating DEAs as viable soft robotic technology for space applications.

title: ManipulationNet: An Infrastructure for Benchmarking Real-World Robot Manipulation with Physical Skill Challenges and Embodied Multimodal Reasoning
comment: 32 pages, 8 figures
summary: Dexterous manipulation enables robots to purposefully alter the physical world, transforming them from passive observers into active agents in unstructured environments. This capability is the cornerstone of physical artificial intelligence. Despite decades of advances in hardware, perception, control, and learning, progress toward general manipulation systems remains fragmented due to the absence of widely adopted standard benchmarks. The central challenge lies in reconciling the variability of the real world with the reproducibility and authenticity required for rigorous scientific evaluation. To address this, we introduce ManipulationNet, a global infrastructure that hosts real-world benchmark tasks for robotic manipulation. ManipulationNet delivers reproducible task setups through standardized hardware kits, and enables distributed performance evaluation via a unified software client that delivers real-time task instructions and collects benchmarking results. As a persistent and scalable infrastructure, ManipulationNet organizes benchmark tasks into two complementary tracks: 1) the Physical Skills Track, which evaluates low-level physical interaction skills, and 2) the Embodied Reasoning Track, which tests high-level reasoning and multimodal grounding abilities. This design fosters the systematic growth of an interconnected network of real-world abilities and skills, paving the path toward general robotic manipulation. By enabling comparable manipulation research in the real world at scale, this infrastructure establishes a sustainable foundation for measuring long-term scientific progress and identifying capabilities ready for real-world deployment.

AI.motivation: Despite decades of advances in robotics hardware, perception, control, and learning, progress toward general manipulation systems remains fragmented due to the absence of widely adopted standard benchmarks. The central challenge is reconciling real-world variability with the reproducibility and authenticity required for rigorous scientific evaluation.

AI.result: Establishes a persistent and scalable infrastructure that enables comparable manipulation research in the real world at scale. Creates a sustainable foundation for measuring long-term scientific progress and identifying capabilities ready for real-world deployment.
AI.conclusion: ManipulationNet addresses the critical need for standardized real-world benchmarks in robotic manipulation, fostering systematic growth of interconnected abilities and skills, and paving the path toward general robotic manipulation by enabling rigorous, reproducible evaluation in unstructured environments.
